In destination storage (ordinary room) at about 32 °C and 75% RH (assumed), this pack keeps it below the limit for about 621 days (cautious estimate 349 days); you need 15 days. Oxygen: about 4.87 mg enters over the period against a tolerance of 2.50 mg per pack. It applies only if: About 75.3 mg O₂ is available to the food (headspace + ingress) vs a long-storage tolerance of 2.50 mg. For 15 days this is treated as acceptable because oxidation is slow over short periods — an assumption (≤ 30 days) to confirm by sensory check. Clear pack: keep in a closed outer carton and store away from light.

checks.message: Room temperature/humidity assumed from destination climate. A ₹300 thermo-hygrometer reading would replace this assumption.

checks.label: Note
checks.message: Broken pieces oxidise faster than wholes (larger surface).

checks.label: Note
checks.message: Roasting increases oxidation rate — treat roasted kernels as more oxygen-sensitive.

checks.label: Initial moisture
checks.message: Reference estimate, not a batch measurement. Measuring the batch (oven-drying or a moisture meter) narrows the uncertainty.

checks.label: Sorption isotherm
checks.message: Linearised isotherm — illustrative until replaced by a sourced or measured isotherm.

checks.label: Oxygen tolerance
checks.message: Class-level tolerance (textbook table). A product-specific limit needs a storage study (peroxide value / sensory).

needs.text: Keep moisture below 5% (w.b.). Moisture above the UNECE limit softens kernels and raises mould risk.
High fat content (~45%) — oxygen drives rancidity.
Light accelerates colour loss / oxidation — opaque pack or dark outer carton.
Hermetic closure prevents insect entry; avoid tie-closures for storage.

requirements.label: Required WVTR (0.5 kg pack, 150 days)

requirements.label: Required OTR (0.5 kg pack, 150 days)
requirements.basis: 23 °C / 0% RH test condition; oxygen-budget method (tolerable O₂ gain ÷ exposure-weighted ingress per unit OTR).

candidates.explanation: Recyclable-design polythene zip pouch with a thin oxygen-barrier layer (PE / EVOH 4 / PE 100 µm (mono-PE design)) in 1 kg packs (30 packs), sent by shared-load goods transport (part load). It is the same kind of pack as supermarket dry fruit and seed packs such as Nutraj, Happilo. Your cashew kernels must stay below 5% moisture. In destination storage (ordinary room) at about 32 °C and 75% RH (assumed), this pack keeps it below the limit for about 161 days (cautious estimate 89 days); you need 151 days. Oxygen is controlled by an oxygen absorber; about 117 mg enters through the film against a tolerance of 10.0 mg. It applies only if: Clear pack: keep in a closed outer carton and store away from light. Still to check: Moisture protection is marginal: conservative estimate 89 days vs target 151 days. Measuring the batch moisture would firm this up.
